author: TEDx Talks
description:
Before Lagos became synonymous with fashion, before African designs walked the runways of Paris and Milan, there was Fagge: a historic community in Kano, northern Nigeria. This is the hidden history of West Africa’s fashion capital

In this powerful talk, we are invited to rethink where innovation truly begins. Through the story of Fagge, Sadiya confronts a bigger global truth: the industries we celebrate are often built by communities the world overlooks. Sadiya Adado is a Nigerian Structural engineer, born and raised in Kano state, a climate justice activist, and a global leader passionate about amplifying the untold stories of marginalised people. As the founder of United Youth for Environmental Sustainability (U-YES), she uses storytelling and creative approaches to bridge awareness and action, ensuring that the voices and issues of the underserved reach the global stage, while bringing global awareness back to the grassroots. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conf
title: How My Community Sewed a Nation’s Style but Lost the Credit | Sadiya Adado | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
African cities are often labelled “informal,” “chaotic,” or “unplanned.” But hidden in these streets, homes, and structures is a profound intelligence, a way of living, adapting, and surviving that teaches us how to design resilient, sustainable, and just cities. In Olorunfemi's talk, he shares how he discovered that architecture can learn from informality, memory, and community to shape the cities of the future. Olorunfemi Adewuyi is an architectural designer and researcher based in Lagos, Nigeria. He founded Omi Collective (2023), an antidisciplinary design and research group. Omi—meaning “water” in Yoruba, his mother tongue—reflects a sustained engagement with the politics and poetics of this resource.

He is attuned to identifying latent and dismissed intelligences, reframing them to broaden the often resistive canons of modernity into a more inclusive whole. Adewuyi is the recipient of notable fellowships and awards, including the Prince Claus Building Beyond Fellowship (2025), I
title: What Informal Cities Can Teach the World | Olorunfemi Adewuyi | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the way we learn erases who we are? In many African schools, students memorise history written by outsiders and lose connection to their own stories. In this talk by Paul, discover how African-centred education, rooted in heritage, storytelling, and community, is reclaiming knowledge, shaping confident leaders, and offering a model the world can learn from. Paul Ninson is a Ghanaian founder, executive director, scholar, and visual storyteller whose work bridges art, archives, education, and social transformation. He is the visionary behind the Dikan Centre in Accra, Ghana — home to Africa’s largest photography library and a pioneering institution redefining visual education on the continent.

Founded in 2022, Dikan nurtures Africa’s next generation of creative leaders through education, exhibitions, research, and cultural heritage preservation. Under Paul’s leadership, the Center has expanded into the Awo Institute, a research and digitization hub advancing African-centered sc
title: This is What African-Centred Education Looks Like  | Paul Ninson | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dance isn’t just entertainment.  it’s one of humanity’s oldest and most powerful technologies. From healing trauma to building leadership, connecting communities, and driving creative economies, movement shapes individuals and societies. In this talk, discover how embracing our authentic expressions can transform lives, industries, and the world. Kafayat Oluwatoyin Shafau, known to the world as Kaffy, is a transformational force in the global creative economy.

From breaking theGuinness World Record for the Longest Dance Party to pioneering Africa’s first structured and registered dance company and academy, Kaffy’s
journey has been one of mastery, innovation, and impact.

As a choreographer, creative director, filmmaker, wellness educator, and transformation coach, Kaffy has dedicated her life to proving that movement is more than art—it is a tool for healing, empowerment, and
social change.

Over two decades, she has evolved from an individual performer into a creative entrepreneur,
title: The Hidden Power of Dance  | DR. Kafayat Oluwatoyin Shafau | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In Oyeyemi's talk, discover the African cure for apathy: how family, cultural instruction, and the subtle power of orientation shape citizens long before they reach the ballot box. It’s a fresh way to think about democracy, values, and the role of community in building a stronger nation. Oyeyemi is a lawyer, writer, and policy advisor. She is renowned for speaking and writing on professional, social, and political matters in a way that young people connect with and derive value from.

From the boardroom to the streets, she has championed access and opportunity for young people and women. She leads the Baton Initiative Africa, a social enterprise set up with the essential intent of equipping Africa’s next generation with the right values, skillset, and cultural agility to build and sustain the emerging Africa.

She served as the youngest member of the executive council of the Nigerian Bar Association Section on Business Law and the Nigerian Bar Association Women Forum at the time of he
title: Why Civic Duty Must Start in the Family  | Oyeyemi Aderibigbe | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At 13, Benita survived a kidnapping, but the trauma stayed. In this talk, she shares how poetry became her therapy, her voice, and her path to healing. Discover how writing can help anyone process trauma, reclaim their story, and transform pain into strength. Benita-Maria Kelechi Opara, also known as Rialena, is a first-class graduate of Architecture and an award-winning spoken word artiste with over nine years of experience in poetry and performance. For her, spoken word transcends art—it is a powerful medium for expressing her faith, challenging perspectives and shaping culture as her architectural touch shapes spaces.

Rialena has performed across diverse platforms and audiences. Her piece “I Have Decided” won the 2024 Ekpebiwo’m Spoken Word Challenge, earning acclaim for its depth and delivery.

Beyond architecture and poetry, Rialena is a skilled public speaker who has trained over 100 students in the last two years on effective communication and presentation. She is also an expe
title: How I Wrote My Way Out of Trauma  | Benita-Maria Kelechi Opara | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this hilarious talk, Dr . Ayodele makes an important case for early infant nutrition. He emphasises key reasons why the combination of play and the right nutrition can set a child up well for life.  Dr. Ayodele Renner is a consultant paediatrician with over a decade of experience. He’s also a social media influencer and health content creator, known as “The Noisy Naija Paediatrician” on Instagram, where he shares free healthcare information and education with over 170k followers, reaching 3 million accounts monthly. Dr. Renner is a co-founder of Agnosys Care on Demand, a digital health platform providing tech-driven health solutions, including home immunization services. He’s been nominated for several awards, including “The Force of Wellness” and “Health Influencer of the Year”. He is also Gates Foundation Goal Keeper who advocates for health equity and improved child survival through vaccination and good nutrition. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference form
title: Why Infant Nutrition and Play is Important for The Future   | Dr. Ayodele Renner | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
History forgot to remember disabled lives, and that erasure affects all of us. In this powerful talk, Eva shares her journey of becoming disabled at seventeen and the realisation that society has long erased people like her from memory, museums, textbooks, and online spaces.

Through her movement “The Body as Canvas,” she explores how disability can be preserved and celebrated. Eva Chisom Chukwunelo is a Nigerian storyteller, content creator, and disability inclusion advocate. As an amputee, she uses her personal journey to challenge shame, redefine beauty, and push for accessible and Africanized innovations in fashion, media, and design.

She is deeply passionate about the representation and preservation of disabled persons and their stories, ensuring their voices and experiences remain visible in Africa’s cultural memory. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to Build a World Where Every Body is Worthy of Memory   | Eva Chisom Chukwunelo | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description: Millions in Africa still live without electricity, not because we lack technology, but because we lack skilled people to run it. In this talk, Vincent shares how training human potential can power communities and why investing in people is the most renewable resource we have. Vincent Egoro is Head of Africa Region at the Resource Justice Network, leading advocacy across 30 countries on energy transition, fossil fuel phase-out, and critical minerals. A former architecture student who once studied by candlelight, he champions skills as infrastructure to power Africa’s clean energy future. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to Unlock Earth’s Most Powerful Renewable Resource  | Vincent Egoro | TEDxLagos

author: TEDx Talks
description: For the past 15 years, Erinch has explored what needs to change for businesses to help address the world's social and ecological crises. Is it stronger government regulation, more courageous leadership among CEOs, or greater pressure from consumers and investors? Or is the deeper design of business itself in need of transformation? In this talk, Erinch shares his journey across these approaches and the lessons he has learned about unlocking the transformations our society and planet urgently need from the world of business. Erinch Sahan has spent 20 years leading initiatives across business, civil society, academia and government to transform business. He currently leads the work at the Joseph Rowntree Foundation, where he manages the Foundation’s £430 million investment to promote a just and equitable future. Prior to joining JRF, Erinch spent four years leading a global community of practitioners who apply the concept of Doughnut Economics to the business environment. Erinch has als
title: What's stopping businesses from being a force for good? | Erinch Sahan | TEDxPrague

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the voice that tells you you’re not good enough is not your enemy, but your protector?

In this illuminating and deeply human talk, therapist and researcher Lisa Etherson invites us to reconsider one of our most misunderstood emotions: shame. Drawing from her own life-altering experience of “uncontained shame” and years of clinical work, she reveals how shame is not a personal flaw, but a protective response rooted in our need for attachment and belonging.

Through the lens of her pioneering Shame Containment Theory, Lisa explains how early attachment injuries shape the quiet, persistent shame many of us carry and how perfectionism, imposter syndrome, self-doubt, and avoidance are strategies designed to keep us safe from disconnection. These strategies protect us, yet they can also keep us small.

By understanding shame’s true function, we can transform our inner critic into an inner protector, loosen the grip of limiting patterns, and move toward lives defined not by fear of
title: If you want to change your life, change your relationship with shame | Lisa Etherson | TEDxUWS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We spend a huge part of our lives at work but how often do we stop to consider the energy in the room? Phil Lewis takes us on a candid journey through the highs and lows of workplace dynamics, sharing his own story of failure as a boss and the lessons it taught him about leadership, organisational energy, and human connection.

In this talk, Phil explores why so many workplaces feel like machines optimised for output rather than wellbeing and how leaders often miss the root cause of poor performance: unresolved “injuries” in the system, from the elephant in the room to the hidden hangovers and cupboards under the stairs. Drawing on personal experience, research, and coaching stories, he reveals how organisations are living, learning organisms, and how addressing the unspoken, the difficult, and the uncomfortable can transform energy, productivity, and culture.

This talk is for anyone who’s ever sat in a meeting and felt frustration, fatigue, or hope for something better and wants to
title: This Is How Organisations Heal | Phil Lewis | TEDxUWS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We carry within us voices shaped long before we could understand them voices that tell us we are not enough, not safe, not worthy of love.

In this raw and deeply reflective talk, trauma-informed therapist Sandra Stein explores how these internalized messages from childhood and culture shape our beliefs, behaviours, and sense of self. From patterns of people-pleasing and hiding, to perfectionism and self-criticism, Sandra reveals the hidden cost of living through these protective adaptations.

Through stories from her clinical work, she shows how compassion, self-inquiry, and therapy can transform the inner critic into a source of support. By softening the voice within, we can reconnect with ourselves, heal shame, and nurture authentic belonging.

This talk is a powerful reminder that our inner world shapes everything we do and that true connection begins by meeting ourselves with care.
 Sandra is a Gestalt Humanistic Integrative Counsellor specialising in trauma-informed practice, cr
title: The Voice Inside: Healing Our Inner Dialogue To Reconnect | Sandra Stein | TEDxUWS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this visually engaging and thought-provoking talk, Matas Kardokas explores the evolution of photography in the age of smartphones, social media, and digital perfection. From carefully staged Instagram aesthetics to algorithm-driven trends, he unpacks how technology has quietly reshaped not only how we take photos, but how we see ourselves.

Blending cultural observation with creative insight, Matas examines how filters, editing tools, and online validation influence identity, memory, and authenticity. What was once about capturing moments has increasingly become about crafting perception.

Through powerful examples and sharp analysis, this talk challenges us to question whether we are documenting reality or designing it. More importantly, it invites us to reconsider our relationship with the images we create and consume every day.

In a world saturated with visuals, understanding why photos look the way they do may reveal deeper truths about connection, self-image, and the stories
title: Why do photos look like that now? | Matas Kardokas | TEDxUWS

Na podstawie wieloletniego doświadczenia w pracy ze słowem i komunikacją opowiada o metodzie, która pozwala przełożyć myśli, emocje i relacje na trójwymiarowe modele. Pokazuje, że szczera rozmowa i element zabawy mogą całkowicie zmienić sposób myślenia o współpracy. W trakcie tej wyprawy odkrywa, że długie życie to nie tylko kwestia technologii czy medycyny, ale także codziennych wyborów, sensu życia i relacji z innymi. Marek Piotrowski to filmowiec i strateg marketingowy, który po latach pracy dla globalnych marek postanowił skupić się na tym, co naprawdę fundamentalne - jak żyć dłużej, zdrowiej i pełniej. Jest twórcą projektu Live Beyond, w ramach którego bada, jak łączyć naukę, technologię i codzienne nawyki w praktyczne podejście do długowieczności. Wraz ze swoim synem przemierzył pięć kontynentów i 39 krajów, rozmawiając z ponad setką naukowców, lekarzy i ekspertów, od Harvardu i Stanforda
title: Żyj Więcej. Podróż po długowieczność | Marek Piotrowski | TEDxSGH

description: In this inspiring TEDx talk, Marit takes us beyond the medals to explore what it truly means to win from within. Through personal stories of challenge and triumph, she reveals how mindset, resilience, and inner strength shape performance when it matters most. A powerful reflection on perseverance and passion, this talk reminds us that real victory begins long before the finish line. Marit Bouwmeester is a Dutch professional sailor and widely regarded as the most successful female Olympic sailor in history. A four-time Olympic medallist who won silver at London 2012, gold at Rio 2016, bronze at Tokyo 2020 and gold at Paris 2024, she has also claimed multiple world and European titles. Drawing on a career built on relentless learning, resilience and high-pressure performance, she now shares her experience as a keynote speaker and performance expert, focusing on mindset and the mental side of winning. Through the Marit Bouwmeester Academy, she is committed to making watersports accessibl

description: In this heartfelt and thought-provoking talk, she explores how healing goes far beyond medicine and why humour still belongs in even the most serious moments. By showing how Artificial Intelligence can take on the science, she makes a case for keeping humanity, empathy, and laughter at the center of care. Get ready for a talk that redefines what it means to heal and connect. Dr. Sabine Fonderson is a Dutch general practitioner, researcher and healthtech advisor. After many years working in A&E for the NHS in the UK, she completed a Master’s in Paediatric Emergency Medicine at the University of Edinburgh. She now runs her own GP practice near Rotterdam and is a PhD candidate at Erasmus MC, where she studies why children visit their GP and how factors like air pollution and socio-economic status drive health inequalities. Alongside her clinical work, she designs digital health tools, advises startups on safe clinical workflows, and hosts the “Doctors in Court” podcast, helping doctors n
title: The art of medicine | Sabine Fonderson | TEDxHotelschool The Hague

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this engaging talk, Jasper and Theo share how two distinct journeys converged into one powerful story of collaboration and growth. Through reflection and shared experience, they show how unexpected connections can ignite creativity, broaden perspective, and inspire lasting change. A heartfelt reminder that when paths cross, new possibilities begin. Jasper Riehm and Theo Rekelhof are the co-founders of ThatWeirdPlantGuy / Rooted in Nature, a creative studio that turns urban spaces into living green sanctuaries. Executive chef turned bio-artist, Jasper combines culinary precision with a love for living architecture to create immersive plant-based installations. Theo, an environmental artist and activist, is dedicated to the emancipation of nature and ensures every design merges creativity with ecological harmony. title: From strangers to a living network! | Jasper Riehm & Theo Rekelhof | TEDxHotelschool The Hague

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world increasingly driven by artificial intelligence, automation, and algorithms, we are learning to code machines to think, decide, and even create. But as technology advances at an extraordinary pace, an important question emerges: what is the one line of code machines still cannot replicate?

In this thought-provoking talk, the speaker explores the idea that while we can program intelligence, efficiency, and logic, the most essential element of progress is still deeply human empathy, compassion, and moral judgment. These qualities cannot simply be written into an algorithm.

By reflecting on the intersection of technology and humanity, this talk challenges us to rethink our role in a rapidly evolving digital world. It reminds us that the future is not just about smarter machines, but about wiser humans who design them.

Ultimately, the talk invites us to consider that the most important code shaping our future may not exist in machines at all it exists within us. I am a curiou
title: The Missing Line Of Code: Humanity | THEOLA R | TEDxMSAJCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
On the TEDx stage, Jasper van Luit invites us to question what we think we know. Through captivating illusions and interactive experiments, he reveals how easily our minds can miss what’s right in front of us, from counting mistakes to reading nonsense effortlessly. His talk uncovers how often we live on autopilot, encouraging us to slow down, see differently, and open our minds to new ways of thinking and creating. Jasper van Luit is a contemporary magician who combines classic magic with modern storytelling. His performances focus on creating meaningful experiences rather than just visual spectacle, using psychology, timing, and audience interaction to bring moments of wonder to life.

From an early age, Jasper was fascinated by how perception shapes reality, a curiosity that continues to influence his refined and immersive style. Whether performing close-up magic or on stage, he aims to connect personally with his audience and make the impossible feel real.

title: Seeing Isn’t Knowing | Jasper van Luit | TEDxHotelschool The Hague

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this inspiring talk, Ludwig Sambo takes us on a journey from his roots in Curaçao through his evolving career in hospitality. By stepping into different fields and embracing unexpected detours, he reveals how each experience shaped his inner compass for navigating life and work and how following curiosity can lead to meaningful direction.

 Hospitality is not just my career it’s my calling. With 18+ years of experience in the industry, I’ve specialized in developing, training, and coaching individuals and teams to deliver excellence in service and leadership. From leading hotel operations to mentoring future hospitality leaders, I thrive on empowering people to reach their full potential.

My mission is to inspire and equip the next generation with the skills, confidence, and mindset they need to succeed in this fast-evolving industry. Whether on the floor, in the classroom, or behind the scenes, I bring energy, structure, and a hands-on leadership style that connects with people.
title: Why experience is your inner compass | Ludwig Sambo | TEDxHotelschool The Hague

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do some moments bring out the best in us while others make us doubt ourselves? The difference often lies in a small but powerful shift happening inside our minds.

In this thought-provoking talk, the speaker explores the invisible “switch” within each of us the inner mindset that determines whether we step forward with confidence or retreat with fear. Through relatable experiences and powerful insights, the talk reveals how self-belief, environment, and the stories we tell ourselves influence our ability to shine.

By understanding how this inner switch works, we can learn to take control of it. Instead of shrinking in moments of uncertainty, we can choose courage, growth, and possibility. This talk invites the audience to recognize their own hidden potential and realize that the power to shine has always been within them. title: The Switch Inside You: Why We Shine Or Shrink | Syed Muhammed Junaid | TEDxMSAJCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"The Paper Crown" explores the emotional reality behind modern achievement, where success often feels fragile, temporary, or undeserved. Living in a world defined by metrics, comparison, and constant validation, many of us wear our confidence like a crown, but it's paper-thin. This talk decodes Imposter Syndrome in the "now" of how high achievers can seem accomplished yet internally doubt their worth, how identity becomes tied to performance, and how we might move from performing success to actually living it. The Paper Crown isn't about breaking, instead it's about recognizing our value beyond applause and learning to replace fragile validation with grounded self-belief.

I chose “The Paper Crown” because it so effectively exemplifies how success often appears strong from without, but sometimes feels incredibly fragile from within. There were times when I did accomplish things , yet felt as though I didn't deserve them. The title reflects that feeling , wearing confidence that looks
title: The Paper Crown | Dhersheni M | TEDxMSAJCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world increasingly shaped by automation, artificial intelligence, and digital perfection, the essence of humanity often feels overlooked. Technology strives for flawless performance but humans are defined by something very different: our imperfections.

In “Imperfectly Perfect: The Art of Humanity Where It Doesn’t Exist,” Sathvika B explores how empathy, emotion, creativity, and vulnerability remain uniquely human qualities in spaces dominated by machines and systems. She reflects on how our flaws, mistakes, and unpredictability are not weaknesses but the very elements that make us authentic and meaningful.

This talk invites the audience to rethink perfection and embrace the beauty of being human. Because in places where humanity seems absent, it is often our imperfections that bring the most powerful sense of connection and purpose. title: Imperfectly Perfect: The Art Of Humanity Where It Doesn't Exist | Sathvika B | TEDxMSAJCE

description:
Life often presents us with moments of uncertainty—those “Are you sure?” crossroads where a single decision can reshape the direction of our lives. But what happens when the roles we identify with, the strengths we rely on, and the comforts we hold onto suddenly disappear? When everything familiar is stripped away, how do we rediscover who we truly are? Dr. Sumedha Bajpai is an eminent educationist, certified international trainer, and founder who has dedicated over two decades to shaping minds and transforming institutions. She is currently serving as Head, School of Business & Management at Jaipur National University, Jaipur, where she leads with a vision grounded in innovation, impact, and inclusivity.

Dr. Bajpai has earlier held key academic leadership roles as Dean and Director, and has trained thousands of students, educators, and professionals in areas like Emotional Intelligence, Employability Skills, Business Communication, and Leadership Development. She is the creator of a
title: Designing Life in Uncertainty | Dr Sumedha Bajpai | TEDxHimalayan International School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In the digital age, many of our choices what we watch, buy, read, and even believe are quietly influenced by algorithms. These invisible systems analyze our behavior, predict our preferences, and guide our decisions in ways we often don’t notice.

In “The Pause Inside Us: How Algorithms Shape What We Choose,” Sania explores how recommendation systems, social media feeds, and digital platforms shape our daily choices. More importantly, she introduces the idea of the pause the moment of awareness where we stop, question, and consciously decide rather than simply follow what technology suggests.

This talk invites the audience to rethink their relationship with technology and reclaim their power of choice. Because in a world driven by algorithms, the most powerful tool we still have is the human ability to pause, reflect, and choose with intention. title: The Pause Inside Us: How Algorithms Shape What We Choose | Sania Masood | TEDxMSAJCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this inspiring talk, Sandeep Singh shares the extraordinary journey behind one of Indian sport’s most remarkable comebacks. From becoming one of the world’s most feared drag-flick specialists to navigating multiple career-threatening injuries, his story is a powerful lesson in resilience, discipline, and belief. Through relentless training, unwavering willpower, and a deep focus on what lies within our control, he fought his way back to the international stage and continued to lead by example. Through his experiences, he reflects on the importance of discipline, mental strength, and perseverance, showing how setbacks and challenges can become the very forces that shape champions.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. title: Ek Sapne Se Soorma Tak | Sandeep Singh | TEDxDepartment Of Commerce

description:
This talk explores how social media influences and manipulates our thoughts, emotions, and daily behavior without us realizing it. As students, we spend a lot of time online, often believing we are in control. Through simple examples and real-life observations, this talk highlights how likes, trends, and algorithms affect our self-esteem, decisions, and attention. The aim is to create awareness and encourage young people to use social media more mindfully instead of being unconsciously controlled by it.

I was inspired to pick this title by my own experiences and observations as a student. I noticed how social media affects the way students think, feel, and compare themselves with others. Many of us unknowingly change our opinions, behavior, and self-worth based on likes, views, and trends. Seeing how powerful this influence is made me curious to understand it better.
